title: weighted-lint-router-and-zero-noise-release-schedule
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: our monorepo lint pipeline has grown noisy and causes long presubmit latency for low-risk changes. This PR implements a lightweight, priority-aware lint router that routes presubmit jobs into weighted lanes (fast, default, full) based on file-path globs, historical flakiness, and change size. It also introduces a quiet release schedule hook (release-shelf) that batches non-critical release hooks into a low-noise window to reduce release churn and pager interruptions. Motivation: improve developer feedback time for common edits, reduce CI cost by avoiding full-lint runs when not necessary, and provide a safe, observable path for release automation that minimizes interrupts during business hours. Scope: - New router service (Go microservice) with simple config maps and a default rule set. - CI workflow changes: presubmit YAMLs now call the router to select a lint job profile. - Release hook orchestration changes: a release-shelf controller groups release-related notifications and triggers for low-priority tasks. - Tests: unit tests for router logic, integration smoke for selected repos, end-to-end presubmit simulation harness. Single-line summary of config example: "{\"fast\": [\"**/*.md\",\"docs/**\"], \"full\": [\"**/*.go\",\"**/*.py\"]}" Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4982 - [x] Router unit tests (coverage 88%) - [x] Presubmit workflow update and backwards-compatible default - [x] Release-shelf controller with opt-in toggle - [x] Observability: added metrics and tracing spans - [x] Manual QA: simulated 500 presubmit events with expected lane split Results: median presubmit latency reduced from 3.7m to 1.2m for fast-lane changes; CI compute used for lint decreased ~22% across sampled week. Commits summary: - Add weighted lint router microservice (pkg/router, cmd/router) - Wire presubmit workflows to router and add fast/default/full job profiles - Add release-shelf controller and opt-in toggle for repos - Add tests, metrics, and docs - Fix race in lint cache priming (follow-up) Changed files (high-level): - ci/presubmit/*.yaml - infra/router/cmd/main.go - infra/router/pkg/router/* - infra/release/release_shelf_controller.go - docs/ci/weighted-lint.md - tools/presubmit/simulate_presubmits.sh - Makefile Review conversation: Miguel: "Can we ensure fallback to full-run on unknown patterns?" (requested changes) Aisha: "Yes — added default fallback and explicit opt-out flag; tests added." Priya: "Observability looks good, can we add a dashboard panel for lane distribution?" (approved after addition) Oliver: "Minor nit: rename fast->quick in doc examples to avoid confusion with fast CI runners." (addressed) CI: initial runs had a flaky e2e check (presubmit simulator) — rerun fixed it; all checks green on final push. Notes on rollout: - Feature gated behind repo-level opt-in label "ci:weighted-lint" - Default behavior unchanged for repos that do not opt in - Rolling rollout plan: start with docs, examples repos, then service, then core runtime repos Related work: ties to ENG-5010 (presubmit cost quotas) and to previous lint-router experiments. Merge: squash-merged to main with conventional-changelog style commit message. Release notes: "Add priority-aware lint routing to reduce presubmit latency and lower lint compute. Introduces an opt-in release-shelf to batch low-priority release hooks and quiet noisy release notifications." Operational runbook (short): - To opt a repo in: add label "ci:weighted-lint" or set repo config in infra/router/config.yaml - To revert: remove label; router will fallback to legacy behavior - Observability: metric router_lane_distribution.*, traces under infra.router span. Follow-ups planned: - Add machine-learned heuristics for historical flakiness in a follow-up (ENG-5122) - Add optional prewarm for quick-lane cache to further reduce latency - Expand release-shelf rules to support cron windows and timezone-aware quiet windows
